newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Sept 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Sept 27.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The 7.23 billion crown surplus from the 1995 state budget will most likely be put into the state reserves. In this way the surplus will help in the fight against inflation. Parliament should come to a final decision on the use of the surplus in its upcoming meeting.

- Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus left on a 4-day official visit to the U.S. During his visit Klaus will meet with US foreign minister, Warren Christopher and the chairman of the World Bank, James Wolfensohn. He will also be giving a series of lectures.

- Some banks are trying to decrease the volume of their primary deposits in order to lower the obligatory minimum reserves, according to a number of bank specialists. One way to do this is to offer products which appear to be secondary deposits which have no relation to the minimum reserves.

- Ceska Rafinerska a.s., the Czech fuel production monopoly, increased its share of the petrol market by 39 percent in the first half of this year and of the diesel fuel market by 45 percent. In this period the company sold 809 thousand tonnes of petrol and 1.11 million tons of diesel fuel.
- Approximately two-thirds of Czech exports are sent to EU countries, half of this total for Germany alone.

- A twelve-year contract between China and Tatra for the manufacturing of lorries in China is running out this year and Tatra has no guarantee that the company wil be able to continue this manufacturing in the future.

- The largest Czech importer and exporter of textiles and clothing, Centrotex, has obtained a majority share in its third textile plant. Centrotex now has a controlling interest in Perla Usti nad Orlici, Beba Broumov and Slezan Frydek-Mistek.

- Tesla Television a.s. plans to expand its market share in the Czech Republic to 30 percent in 1997. The company posted a turnover of 250 million crowns and a slight profit in 1995 on sales of approximately 25 thousand televisions.

- The largest domestic lottery office, Sazka, posted record turnover and profit in 1995. The company's net profit of 650.2 million crowns places it among the top ten largest enterprises in th country interms of profit. The company posted a turnover of 3.976 billion crowns.
PRAVO - The Central Election Commission has refused nearly 100 of the 570 senatorial candidates on the basis of small technicalities causing a wave of protest and appeals to the High Court.

- The Czech Republic, with 70 functioning breweries (not including micro-breweries), is in fifth place in Europe in terms of number of breweries. In terms of beer production, the Czech Republic is in sixth place with 17.855 hectolitres a year. In terms of per capita consumption, however, The Czech Republic is in first place with 159 litres followed by Germany with 138 litres.
